quests.sentence: When the phone rang, I was cooking dinner.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was cooking is the past progressive form, describing the ongoing background action interrupted by the ringing phone.
quests.nativeTip: One action was already underway when the phone interrupted it.
quests.example: When the phone rang, I was cooking dinner.

quests.sentence: When the phone rang, I answered it immediately.
quests.ruleExplanation: Answered is the simple past form, describing a quick reaction that followed the previous event.
quests.nativeTip: These two actions happened right after each other, not at overlapping times.
quests.example: When the phone rang, I answered it immediately.

quests.sentence: When I got home, my roommate had already cooked dinner.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had cooked is the past perfect form, showing the action was complete before another past event.
quests.nativeTip: The cooking was finished before I even arrived home.
quests.example: When I got home, my roommate had already cooked dinner.

quests.sentence: While I was cooking dinner, my roommate set the table.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was cooking is the past progressive form, describing the ongoing background action while another action took place.
quests.nativeTip: Focus on the background action that was already happening.
quests.example: While I was cooking dinner, my roommate set the table.

quests.sentence: While the kids do their homework, I usually prepare dinner.
quests.ruleExplanation: Do and prepare are simple present forms, describing two habitual actions that regularly happen at the same time.
quests.nativeTip: Both halves describe a repeated daily pattern, not a specific moment.
quests.example: While the kids do their homework, I usually prepare dinner.

quests.sentence: While the manager was presenting the new plan, several employees were exchanging skeptical glances.
quests.ruleExplanation: Were exchanging is the past progressive form, describing an action happening simultaneously with another ongoing past action.
quests.nativeTip: Two actions were happening at the same time in the past.
quests.example: While the manager was presenting the new plan, several employees were exchanging skeptical glances.

quests.sentence: Before the movie started, we grabbed some popcorn.
quests.ruleExplanation: Grabbed is the simple past form, describing an action whose order is already clear from the word 'before'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Before' already makes the order between these two actions clear.
quests.example: Before the movie started, we grabbed some popcorn.

quests.sentence: After we'd grabbed popcorn, we could barely find two seats together.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had grabbed (shortened to 'd grabbed) is the past perfect form, emphasizing that the action was complete before the next situation.
quests.nativeTip: This stresses that the popcorn run was fully finished before the seating problem.
quests.example: After we'd grabbed popcorn, we could barely find two seats together.

quests.sentence: We looked for seats after the trailers had already begun.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had begun is the past perfect form, showing the trailers started before the later past action of searching for seats.
quests.nativeTip: The trailers were already running before we started looking for seats.
quests.example: We looked for seats after the trailers had already begun.

quests.sentence: By the time the ambulance reached the scene, bystanders had already cleared the road.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had cleared is the past perfect form, showing the road was cleared before a later past event.
quests.nativeTip: This action was complete before the ambulance's arrival.
quests.example: By the time the ambulance reached the scene, bystanders had already cleared the road.

quests.sentence: By the time we finish this project, we'll have redesigned the entire website twice.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will have redesigned is the future perfect form, describing a total expected to be complete by a future point.
quests.nativeTip: This total will be reached by a future point in time.
quests.example: By the time we finish this project, we'll have redesigned the entire website twice.

quests.conceptTitle: Timeline Mapping: Past Perfect Progressive Tense
quests.sentence: By the time the meeting ended, everyone had been sitting in that stuffy room for three hours.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had been sitting is the past perfect progressive form, emphasizing duration leading up to a later past event.
quests.nativeTip: This measures how long a situation had been continuing before the meeting's end.
quests.example: By the time the meeting ended, everyone had been sitting in that stuffy room for three hours.

quests.sentence: I haven't spoken to him since we argued last month.
quests.ruleExplanation: Haven't spoken is the present perfect form, and since marks the starting point of a situation continuing to the present.
quests.nativeTip: This situation has continued from that past argument right up to now.
quests.example: I haven't spoken to him since we argued last month.

quests.sentence: We waited in the lobby until the doctor finally called our name.
quests.ruleExplanation: Waited is the simple past form, describing an action that continued until a past endpoint.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a finished sequence of events, entirely in the past.
quests.example: We waited in the lobby until the doctor finally called our name.

quests.conceptTitle: Timeline Mapping: Simple Present (Future Time Clause)
quests.sentence: I won't sign anything until my lawyer reviews it.
quests.ruleExplanation: Reviews is the simple present form used for future meaning inside a time clause beginning with until.
quests.nativeTip: Even though the meaning is future, notice that 'will' isn't used in the until-clause itself.
quests.example: I won't sign anything until my lawyer reviews it.

quests.conceptTitle: Timeline Mapping: Simple Present (Future Time Clause)
quests.sentence: I'll text you as soon as I land.
quests.ruleExplanation: Land is the simple present form used for future meaning inside a time clause beginning with as soon as.
quests.nativeTip: The main clause uses will, but the as-soon-as clause doesn't.
quests.example: I'll text you as soon as I land.

quests.sentence: Whenever it rains, the basement floods.
quests.ruleExplanation: Rains and floods are simple present forms, describing a general habitual cause-and-effect pattern.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a general pattern that happens every time the condition is met, not one future event.
quests.example: Whenever it rains, the basement floods.

quests.conceptTitle: Timeline Mapping: Simple Present (Future Time Clause)
quests.sentence: As soon as the results come in, we'll know how to proceed.
quests.ruleExplanation: Come in is the simple present form used for future meaning inside a time clause beginning with as soon as.
quests.nativeTip: The result is still in the future, but the time clause itself avoids will.
quests.example: As soon as the results come in, we'll know how to proceed.

quests.conceptTitle: Timeline Mapping: Simple Present (Future Time Clause)
quests.sentence: When I finish this call, I'll join you.
quests.ruleExplanation: Finish is the simple present form used for future meaning inside a time clause beginning with when.
quests.nativeTip: The joining is a future plan, but notice the verb form right after 'when'.
quests.example: When I finish this call, I'll join you.

quests.sentence: When she finished the call, she joined us in the kitchen.
quests.ruleExplanation: Finished and joined are simple past forms, describing two sequential completed actions.
quests.nativeTip: Both actions are simply reported in the order they happened.
quests.example: When she finished the call, she joined us in the kitchen.

quests.sentence: When she'd finished the call, her whole mood seemed to change.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had finished (shortened to 'd finished) is the past perfect form, showing the call ended before the change that followed.
quests.nativeTip: The finishing happened just before the change in mood, an earlier point in the past.
quests.example: When she'd finished the call, her whole mood seemed to change.

quests.sentence: As soon as I saw the missed calls, I knew something was wrong.
quests.ruleExplanation: Saw and knew are simple past forms, describing two events that happened right after each other.
quests.nativeTip: This is an immediate reaction described as a simple sequence of past events.
quests.example: As soon as I saw the missed calls, I knew something was wrong.

quests.sentence: I'd barely sat down when my phone started buzzing again.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had barely sat down (shortened to 'd barely sat down) is the past perfect form, emphasizing an action just completed before a sudden interruption.
quests.nativeTip: This stresses just how little time had passed before the interruption.
quests.example: I'd barely sat down when my phone started buzzing again.

quests.sentence: Whenever my phone buzzes like that, I assume it's bad news.
quests.ruleExplanation: Buzzes and assume are simple present forms, describing a habitual pattern of reaction.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a repeated personal reaction, not one specific event.
quests.example: Whenever my phone buzzes like that, I assume it's bad news.

quests.sentence: The team won't launch the app until every bug has been fixed.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has been fixed is the present perfect form, used inside the until-clause to stress completion rather than simple future time.
quests.nativeTip: This clause emphasizes that the fixing must be complete before the launch, not an ongoing process.
quests.example: The team won't launch the app until every bug has been fixed.

quests.sentence: By the time customers notice the bug, our team will have already released a fix.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will have released is the future perfect form, describing a task expected to be complete before a future event.
quests.nativeTip: The fix will be finished before customers even notice the problem, a future reference point.
quests.example: By the time customers notice the bug, our team will have already released a fix.

quests.conceptTitle: Timeline Mapping: Present Perfect Progressive Tense
quests.sentence: Ever since the last outage, the team has been monitoring the servers around the clock.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has been monitoring is the present perfect progressive form, emphasizing continuous activity from a past point to now.
quests.nativeTip: This emphasizes an ongoing activity that has continued since that past event.
quests.example: Ever since the last outage, the team has been monitoring the servers around the clock.

quests.sentence: By the time the review board meets, the committee will have already interviewed every candidate twice.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will have interviewed is the future perfect form, describing a task expected to be finished before a future event.
quests.nativeTip: This total will be complete before the board's meeting, a future reference point.
quests.example: By the time the review board meets, the committee will have already interviewed every candidate twice.

quests.sentence: The committee had interviewed most candidates before a scheduling conflict forced them to postpone the final two.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had interviewed is the past perfect form, showing most of the process was finished before a later past disruption.
quests.nativeTip: Most of the interviewing was already complete before the conflict arose.
quests.example: The committee had interviewed most candidates before a scheduling conflict forced them to postpone the final two.

quests.sentence: Whenever a scheduling conflict comes up, the committee simply adjusts the calendar without much fuss.
quests.ruleExplanation: Comes up and adjusts are simple present forms, describing a general habitual response.
quests.nativeTip: This describes their usual, repeated way of handling such situations.
quests.example: Whenever a scheduling conflict comes up, the committee simply adjusts the calendar without much fuss.
